The story skillfully balances the compression and stretching of time to serve its character development and emotional arc. The author compresses large spans of time—such as Denise's eleven years at the grocery store, the eleven-month courtship, the wedding, and the three years it takes to build the new business—into single sentences or brief paragraphs. This keeps the narrative moving briskly and establishes the broader context of Denise's life without bogging the story down in unnecessary detail. 

Conversely, the narrative slows down to "stretch" or dwell on specific, pivotal moments in real-time, such as the initial meeting in the checkout line, the late-night kitchen scene where Denise and Miss Emily fix the velouté recipe, and the negotiation of the business loan. By expanding these brief interactions through dialogue and internal reflection, the writer highlights the subtle shifts in power, respect, and affection between the two women, making the pacing feel deeply intentional and emotionally resonant.
